```{r}
library(broom)
library(PNWColors)
```

## 1. Is medical story related to cardiac events events?

### 1.1 Introduction

Stress echocardiography is used to detect coronary artery disease and to estimate which patients are at risk of future cardiac problems. In the UCLA dataset used here (Garfinkel et al., 1999), 558 patients had a dobutamine stress echocardiogram and were followed for one year. During follow-up we recorded whether each patient had a new heart attack, an angioplasty, bypass surgery or died of cardiac causes. We combine these into a single outcome, "any event".

Before the test, each patient"s medical history was recorded: **hypertension**, **diabetes**, **smoking**, **prior heart attack**, **prior angioplasty** and **prior bypass surgery**. Established heart disease and cardiovascular risk factors are plausibly linked to more future events.

So, firstly, it is sensible to ask oneself, is a patient's prior history associated with having a cardiac event within one year of the stress test?

We expect a higher event rate in patients with a history of given variable. We first compare event rates for each history factor, then summarise the history in a burden score, and last use logistic regression to check whether the pattern holds after accounting for age and gender. The data are observational, so we can describe associations but not causes.

### 1.2 Data preparation

Despite the data has been already cleaned up, it is sensible to simplify the data set to the variables which are planned to be used.

```{r}
#selecting the significative columns for analysis
medical_h_data <- stressEcho |> 
  select(AnyEvent, RecentMyocardialInfarction, RecentAngioplasty, RecentBypassSurgery, death, HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, SmokingHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory, age, gender)

head(medical_h_data)
```

Also, burden score variable is being created. It will consist on a score given to each patient depending on the presence/absence of the proposed events on their story (Scores go from 0 to 6). Smoking history is divided in three categories: `non-smokers`, `moderate` and `heavy`. For the purpose of our analysis, we are simplifying to `non-smokers` and `smokers`.

```{r}
#convert yes/no to 1/0 for summing up the number of patients with certain history
medical_h_data <- medical_h_data |>
  mutate(
      HypertensionHistory = case_when(HypertensionHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                      HypertensionHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      DiabetesHistory = case_when(DiabetesHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                  DiabetesHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      MyocardialInfarctionHistory = case_when(MyocardialInfarctionHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                              MyocardialInfarctionHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      AngioplastyHistory = case_when(AngioplastyHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                     AngioplastyHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      BypassSurgeryHistory = case_when(BypassSurgeryHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                       BypassSurgeryHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      SmokingHistory = case_when(SmokingHistory == "non-smoker" ~ 0,
                                 SmokingHistory == "heavy" ~ 1,
                                 SmokingHistory == "moderate" ~ 1),
      AnyEvent = case_when(AnyEvent == "yes" ~ 1,
                                       AnyEvent == "no" ~ 0),
    HistoryBurden = HypertensionHistory + DiabetesHistory + AngioplastyHistory + BypassSurgeryHistory + MyocardialInfarctionHistory
  )

head(medical_h_data)
```

### 1.3 Analysis

#### 1.3.1 Does the presence of the different histories affect the number of events in patients?

In the following code, only the essential columns are chosen, data is pivoted longer for facilitating the summary of the whole data set. Two new variables are added to the data set: `n`, being the total number of occurrences for each history condition and presence (`with`) or absence (`without`) and also the `event_rate` being the percentage of the patients with certain condition to have had a cardiac event.

```{r}
medical_h_long_1 <- medical_h_data |>
  select(
    c(HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory, AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory),
    names_to = "History",
    values_to = "Levels"
  ) |> 
  group_by(History, Levels) |> 
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    events = sum(AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    event_rate = (events/n)*100,
    Levels = case_when(
      Levels == 0 ~ "without", 
      Levels == 1 ~ "with"
    )
  )

view(medical_h_long_1)
```

```{r}
overall <- medical_h_data |> 
  summarise(
    mean(AnyEvent) * 100
  )

ggplot(data=medical_h_long_1, aes(x = History, y = event_rate, fill = Levels)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = as.numeric(overall), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25,
                                   hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Medical history",
       y = "Event rate (%)", 
       title = "Events rates in patients with previous medical history") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pnw_palette(name = "Starfish",
                                         n = 2))+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("AngioplastyHistory" = "Angioplasty",
                              "BypassSurgeryHistory" = "Bypass surgery",
                              "DiabetesHistory" = "Diabetes",
                              "HypertensionHistory" = "Hypertension", 
                              "MyocardialInfarctionHistory" = "Myocardical infraction",
                   "SmokingHistory" = "Smoking"))
  
```

#### 1.3.2 Does more history burden increase the probability of an event occurring?

A new subset is created. This time, `HistoryBurden` variable is added to know if the accumulation of events along the history of the patients increases the event rate. If more than 4 events happen, we accumulate them in an united variable `4+` since not many patients have suffered that much events.

```{r}
medical_h_long_2 <- medical_h_data |>
  select(
    c(HistoryBurden, HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory, AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    HistoryBurden = ifelse(HistoryBurden >= 4,
                           "4+",
                           as.character(HistoryBurden))
  ) |> 
  group_by(HistoryBurden) |> 
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    events = sum(AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    event_rate = (events/n)*100,
  )

view(medical_h_long_2)
```

```{r}
overall <- medical_h_data |> 
  summarise(
    mean(AnyEvent) * 100
  )

ggplot(data=medical_h_long_2, aes(x = HistoryBurden, y = event_rate)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", fill=pnw_palette(name = "Starfish", n=1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = as.numeric(overall), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(x="History burden",
       y="Event rate (%)",
       title = "Event rates in patients with accumulative history")
```

#### 1.3.3 Which variable has more effect on the occurrence of any cardiac event?

Finally, a regression model is trained with our data to find out which out of all the variables chosen have a bigger effect on the occurrence of a cardiac event. These findings are presented in a forest plot as well as a data table.

```{r}
library(broom)

model <- medical_h_data |> 
  glm(formula = AnyEvent ~ age + gender + HypertensionHistory + DiabetesHistory + AngioplastyHistory + BypassSurgeryHistory + MyocardialInfarctionHistory + SmokingHistory,
      family = binomial, 
      data=_)

forest_plot_data <- model |>
  tidy(conf.int = TRUE,
       exponentiate = TRUE) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")

ggplot(forest_plot_data, mapping = aes(x = estimate,
                       y = fct_reorder(term,
                                       estimate))) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 1,
                   linetype = "dashed") +
        geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(xmin = conf.low,
                                    xmax = conf.high),
                      width = 0.2) +
        geom_pointrange(mapping = aes(xmin = conf.low,
                                      xmax = conf.high)) +
        scale_x_log10() +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
        scale_y_discrete(labels = c("AngioplastyHistory" = "Angioplasty",
                              "BypassSurgeryHistory" = "Bypass surgery",
                              "DiabetesHistory" = "Diabetes",
                              "HypertensionHistory" = "Hypertension", 
                              "MyocardialInfarctionHistory" = "Myocardical infraction",
                   "SmokingHistory" = "Smoking",
                   "gendermale" = "Male gender",
                   "age" = "Age"))+
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (95% CI, log scale)",
       y=NULL, 
       title = "Adjusted odds ratios for a cardiac event within one year")

view(forest_plot_data)
```
